title: Within Our Gates
description: A Black schoolteacher travels north to raise money for a struggling Southern school for Black children, as the story of her own family's past comes to light. The oldest surviving feature film directed by an African American.
credits: Directed by Oscar Micheaux · Starring Evelyn Preer · Floy Clements · James D. Ruffin

rights.notes: Published before 1931; US copyright term for pre-1978 published works is at most 95 years, so every work published in 1930 or earlier is in the US public domain as of 2026-01-01. US-only conclusion: geo-restrict to the US or clear other territories separately. Released January 1920 by the Micheaux Book & Film Co. RESTORATION CAVEAT (legal review recommended): the only surviving print (the Spanish release 'La negra') was restored by the Library of Congress in 1993; its English intertitles were re-translated from the Spanish by Scott Simmon, then a Library of Congress curator, 'with Spanish-language assistance from Alex Vargas and a previous translation by Kathleen Newman' (on-screen card). Titles written by LoC staff in the course of employment are US Government works (17 USC 105), but the contribution of the outside prior translation is not documented. Video Yesteryear's 1995 registration PA0000741770 claims only 'editing, musical score' (not the film or titles), and the Kino/DJ Spooky score on this file is muted. No other English-titled print exists.

source.notes: Kino Lorber 'Pioneers of African-American Cinema' (2016) encode of the 1993 Library of Congress restoration (1438x1080, H.264, AAC). Head 0-80 s is modern: LoC logo, two 'About the Restoration' text cards and a 'New Musical Score Composed by Paul D. Miller aka DJ Spooky' card; the film starts on the 'Oscar Micheaux presents Within Our Gates' title at ~80.5 s. Tail from ~4387.3 s is modern (score credits, special thanks). The AAC track is the 2016 DJ Spooky score (copyrighted): MUTE it. Same video without audio: silent-within-our-gates/Within Our Gates.mp4 (640x480, 376,926,032 bytes, same timings minus ~0.1 s). title: Eleven P.M.

rights.notes: Published before 1931; US copyright term for pre-1978 published works is at most 95 years, so every work published in 1930 or earlier is in the US public domain as of 2026-01-01. US-only conclusion: geo-restrict to the US or clear other territories separately. Maurice Film Company, Detroit. Usually dated 1928; Bowser and Musser suggest completion as late as 1929 or 1930 (Wikipedia, Richard D. Maurice) - still 1930 or earlier. Belt-and-braces: no registration or renewal exists in the CCE or online records; and even if the film were treated as never published, the author's life+70 term (Maurice died 1955) expired at the end of 2025 (17 USC 303). title: Wealth of a Nation
description: A fast-cut portrait of American freedom of expression, from dissent and debate to art, music, dance, architecture and science, made for overseas audiences by the U.S. Information Agency.
credits: Written, produced and directed by William Greaves · Music by Bill Dixon · A U.S. Information Agency production

rights.notes: USIA film (NARA 306.3957, NAID 50289). The end credits read 'a production of the motion picture and television service of the United States Information Agency', and no copyright notice appears on screen (head and end credits checked). There is no registration in the 1964-1965 CCE motion-picture volumes and no record in the online public records. Greaves (1926-2014, African American documentarian) made it as an independent contractor, not a federal employee, so 17 USC 105 does not apply directly. The basis is publication without notice before 1978, the same reasoning this catalog uses for contractor-made government films such as Private Snafu. NARA's use restriction cites only Public Law 101-246 (domestic release of USIA films 12 years after overseas dissemination, long satisfied). RESIDUAL RISK (counsel sign-off recommended): if the film was disseminated only abroad, some courts (Twin Books v. Disney, 9th Cir. 1996) have held that publication abroad without notice did not divest US copyright. Bill Dixon's commissioned score was published only as part of the film; no separate registration was found.
